Many people ask: since we already have full-text search, vector retrieval, and RAG, why do we still need GitNexus? The key is that code is not ordinary text. Code has clear structure, call relationships, dependency boundaries, and execution paths. Simply slicing code into chunks and retrieving it can easily miss content that does not appear in the same text block but is strongly related logically. A simple way to understand the difference is as follows:
Capability | Keyword Search | General RAG | GitNexus
--- | --- | ---
Search keywords | Yes | Yes | Yes
Find related code snippets | Weak | Yes | Yes
Understand call chains | Needs manual judgment | Unstable | Better suited
Analyze impact scope | Largely experience | Depends on context | Queryable via tools
Serve AI Agent | Indirect | Yes | Natively agent-oriented
GitNexus's core idea can be summarized in one phrase: ** precomputed relationship intelligence **. That is, it first computes code structure, dependency relationships, call chains, functional clusters, and execution flows during the indexing phase. By the time the Agent actually executes a task, what it gets is not a pile of scattered chunks, but a structurally organized project context.

8aaqxt:367: AI coding tools have evolved to the point where they no longer just autocomplete a few lines for you. Tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex are gradually becoming true "partners" that participate in the development process. But in real projects, one problem becomes increasingly obvious: ** AI is not that it can't write code, but that it often can't see the whole code. ** It may understand the current file, yet not know where else a function is called; it may complete a refactoring, yet miss a cross-module dependency; sometimes just changing an inconspicuous return value ends up affecting an entire downstream business flow. GitNexus aims to solve exactly this problem. It first organizes the codebase into a "knowledge graph", pre-analyzing dependency relationships, call chains, functional clusters, and execution flows, and then exposes them to AI Agents via MCP, CLI, Web UI, and other channels. In other words, GitNexus does not make the model "better at guessing"; it makes the model truly understand your codebase before it starts changing code.
